paper.title_en: Characterization of fidelity-based coherences under typical Markovian channels
paper.abstract_en: Quantum coherence serves as a fundamental resource underpinning the functionality of quantum technologies. However, no real quantum system can be fully isolated from its environment, and inevitable system-environment interactions disrupt the superposition of resource states, leading to the degradation of initial coherence. To clarify the impact of environment noise on coherent resources, this study investigates fidelity-based coherences in typical single-qubit Markovian channels. We first calculate the cohering and decohering powers of amplitude damping, phase damping, depolarizing, and flip (bit flip, phase flip, bit-phase flip) channels; these metrics quantify a channel's inherent ability to generate or diminish coherence in quantum systems. We then analyze the decay of fidelity-based coherences for pure state in these Markovian channels. Finally, we demonstrate that weak measurement and reversal measurement can effectively suppress the decohering power of the amplitude damping channel, providing a solid mathematical foundation for regulating coherent resources in open quantum systems.
